chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'a who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man who has a son — does he have the leeway to assign his wealth to his near relatives?' He said: 'It is his wealth; he can do with it whatever he wishes until death comes to him.'

key_terms.الْمَوْت: Death; the moment at which the rules of inheritance (mirath) become operative
key_terms.قَرَابَة: Near relatives, kinsmen; those related by blood or lineage
key_terms.يَسَعُهُ: It is permitted/lawful for him; has the latitude or leeway to do something

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim give his wealth to relatives instead of his children during his lifetime?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the complete and unrestricted right of a person to dispose of their wealth as they see fit during their lifetime, even if they have children. The question posed by Sama'a reflects a practical concern in early Islamic jurisprudence: whether the existence of legal heirs limits a person's freedom to gift or donate wealth before death. The Imam's response establishes a clear principle — ownership rights are fully intact until the moment of death, after which inheritance rules take effect.
